post.description: Create a multi-profile extraction from URL list.

Create a single-profile extraction.

Runs the scrape pipeline inline (not via Dramatiq) so we can return
the serialized prospect in the response, matching the legacy
synchronous behavior at
evaboot_django/public_api/views/extraction.py:1268.

Create a URL-based extraction.

The URL is probed against LinkedIn synchronously before any export
row or Bubble side-effect is created: a query LinkedIn rejects
(400) surfaces as a 422 to the caller, not as an export that fails
30 s later in the worker. Mirrors the extension launcher.

get.description:
Get extraction details by search_id (bubble_id).

Returns 202 + minimal payload for in-progress extractions, 200 + full
payload for completed ones. ``progress`` reports a real percentage —
pagination weighted as the first 75%, parallel scrape as the last
25% — published by the worker to the cache (see
``apps/sales_nav_exports/services/progress.py``). Falls back to 0
when the cache has no entry (legacy exports, dummy cache in tests).

Prospect pagination is opt-in: with ``limit`` omitted the full
``prospects`` array is returned (unchanged). With ``limit`` set only
the ``[start:start+limit]`` page is fetched, and ``total_count`` /
``has_more`` describe the full result set.

Quota + credit information.

Quota is per SalesNav seat (``LinkedInAccount.daily_export_limit``,
default 2500); usage counts profiles each seat launched in the last
24h. Top-level numbers aggregate the user's valid seats; per-seat
detail rides in ``salesnavs``. Without a valid SalesNav account
``remaining`` is 0. Credits come from Django for migrated users,
Bubble otherwise (best-effort, ``0.0`` when Bubble is unreachable).

post.description:
Turn a natural-language request into a Sales Navigator search.

Enforced in order: the daily limit (protects the customer's own LinkedIn
seat from sustained automation — checked before any agent work, not
after), then the Sales Navigator account requirement (same gate every
other extraction endpoint applies).

The daily limit meters **every** turn, not just the ones that go
company-first: a cheap lead-build refinement costs the same unit as a
multi-round company crawl, and a turn that 502s is charged too, since the
increment happens before the agent runs. That is deliberate — every turn
is an Opus call plus typeahead traffic on the customer's own seat, and the
counter must not be refundable by failing on purpose. The practical
consequence is that 20 refinements or 20 errored turns exhaust the day's
company-first budget.

get.description:
Poll a company-first search job. Returns 404 for another user's job.

Deliberately NOT rate-limited by ``DAILY_LIMIT``: a company-first
job runs for minutes and the client polls it every few seconds, so
charging the 20/day agent quota per poll would make polling impossible.
The quota only guards the expensive/automatable POST that starts work.

post.description:
Generate a Sales Navigator URL from a natural-language description.

Free of charge — no credit deduction. Capped at
``SEARCH_BUILDER_DAILY_LIMIT`` calls/day per user (legacy parity).
LLM failures surface as ``GenerationError`` → 400.

get.description:
Poll a search-to-list job.

Tenant-scoped through ``get_for_user``: another customer's job is a 404, not
a 403, so the endpoint never confirms that an id exists.

Deliberately NOT metered by ``SN_SEARCH_TO_LIST_DAILY_LIMIT``: a job runs
for minutes and the client polls it every few seconds, so charging the
launch quota per poll would make polling impossible. The quota guards the
POSTs that start real work.
